newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says interdependent world needs summits.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says interdependent world needs summits.

text.p: President Bill Clinton made his weekly radio address on Saturday from the summit of the Group of Seven industrial nations in Denver and said the global economy's interdependence required countries to work together.
"The very fact that we're gathering speaks volumes about the world today," Clinton said in the radio address.

"Our homelands are thousands of miles apart, but the rise of the global economy ... has brought us all closer together," he said. "Ideas, goods and services, technology and capital all fly across borders faster than ever.

"But while progress spreads quickly ... problems can too," he said. "A currency crisis in one country can send shockwaves far beyond its borders, endangering jobs and stability in a completely different part of the world."

The Group of Seven comprises Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States. Russia is also participating in most of this year's meeting, which has been called the "Summit of the Eight."

Clinton said that one of the summit's aims was to find ways to keep financial crises from spreading, adding that G7 finance ministers had agreed to create a global network of banking and marketing officials to monitor financial policies and to police risky financial practices.
He also said the leaders would seek common strategies to fight the global problems of terrorism, nuclear proliferation, infectious diseases and environmental degradation.
The summit, which began with a working dinner on Friday evening, was scheduled to continue through Sunday, when the leaders will issue a joint communique.
